findings.evidence: Symmetries.lean:157 `∑ s ∈ Species.flavorPair i ∩ C.valence h, D h s z Q2` and ValenceContent.lean:97 `Xor (Species.quark i ∈ C.valence h) (Species.antiquark i ∈ C.valence h)`: no occurrence of `C.conj` or `C.mem_valence_conj` in any of the listed declarations.
findings.fix: Parameterise the splitting on the valence assignment alone — either take `(v : Hadron → Finset (Species Flavor))` in `favored`/`unfavored`/`IsValenceFlavor`/`valenceStepFrag`, or keep only `valence` in `ValenceContent` and make the conjugation compatibility a separate hypothesis (`conj : Hadron → Hadron`, `Function.Involutive conj`, `∀ h s, s ∈ valence (conj h) ↔ Species.conj s ∈ valence h`) supplied by the lemmas that actually need it: `image_conj_inter_valence`, `image_conj_sdiff_valence`, `inter_valence_conj_eq_sdiff`, `sdiff_valence_conj_eq_inter`, `favored_partonConj`, `unfavored_partonConj`, `favored_conj_of_chargeConjRelation`, `unfavored_conj_of_chargeConjRelation`, `IsValenceFlavor.conj`, `chargeConjRelation_valenceStepFrag`.
findings.issue: `favored`, `unfavored` and everything derived from them (`favored_def`…`favored_sub_unfavored_eq_of_antiquark_mem`, `valenceStepFrag` and its five lemmas, and `ValenceContent.IsValenceFlavor` with `isValenceFlavor_iff`, `isValenceFlavor_of_quark_mem`, `isValenceFlavor_of_antiquark_mem`, `antiquark_mem_iff`, `quark_mem_iff` in ValenceContent.lean:95-118) take the full `ValenceContent`, which bundles an antiparticle involution `conj` plus `conj_involutive` and `mem_valence_conj`, but use only `C.valence`. The favoured combination of a hadron whose antiparticle is not in the `Hadron` type (a lone proton or K⁺) cannot be stated at all, since `mem_valence_conj` is unsatisfiable there.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:219-222 uses `hτ` only in `rw [hτ h] at h₁ h₂`; `Function.Involutive.surjective` is at upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/Logic/Function/Basic.lean:1058, so the existing uses (Symmetries.lean:428,437) stay one token longer.
findings.fix: State it as `lemma Invariant.apply_eq_apply (hτ : Function.Surjective τ) …`; obtain `h₀` with `τ h₀ = h` from `hτ h` and rewrite `hσ.apply h₀ i`, `hσ'.apply h₀ i`. The two pion call sites become `Pion.conj_involutive.surjective`.
findings.issue: `Invariant.apply_eq_apply` assumes `Function.Involutive τ`, stronger than the proof needs: it only uses that `h` has a `τ`-preimage. This excludes a flavour relabelling of order > 2 (a cyclic u→d→s permutation induces a 3-cycle on the meson multiplet), for which the conclusion still holds.

findings.evidence: Symmetries.lean:185 `Finset.sum_nonneg fun s _ => hD.nonneg h s z Q2 hz₀ hz₁` is the entire proof; Basic.lean:64 `zMoment_nonneg {D} (hD : ∀ z ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, 0 ≤ D h i z Q2)` takes the pointwise hypothesis rather than `Assumptions`.
findings.fix: Weaken the hypothesis to the pointwise form, e.g. `(hD : ∀ s, 0 ≤ D h s z Q2)`, matching the nearby precedent `zMoment_nonneg`; `Assumptions` users pass `fun s => hD.nonneg h s z Q2 hz₀ hz₁`.
findings.issue: `favored_nonneg` and `unfavored_nonneg` (line 188) take the whole `Assumptions D` bundle but use only `hD.nonneg` at the single `z` of the statement; the `support` field is never used, and the statement is already restricted to `0 ≤ z ≤ 1`.

summary: The favoured/unfavoured splitting is stated over the whole multiplet structure although it only needs the valence assignment, so it cannot be written down for a hadron type not closed under conjugation; `Invariant.apply_eq_apply` assumes an involution where surjectivity suffices, excluding non-involutive flavour permutations.
